items: Restaurant management comes down to people, product and profit: a motivated, well-trained team, a consistent quality product, and numbers tight enough for the business to survive.
Build systems such as opening and closing checklists, prep lists and cross-training before you need them, so service stays consistent whether or not you're on the floor.
Watch food cost, labor cost and daily sales most closely, since small inefficiencies in ingredients and scheduling quickly eat into your margins.
Hire for attitude and coachability, then train skills, and develop people through in-the-moment coaching, clear expectations and recognition of great work.
If you run several locations, standardize recipes and processes, hire strong general managers for each site, and use tools with real-time data to spot problems remotely.
